import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Moser's Worm

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moser%27s_worm_problem)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory

namespace MoserWorm

/--
The set of worms is the set of curves of length (at most) 1.
We formalize this as the set of ranges of 1-Lipschitz functions from `[0,1]` to `ℝ²`.
-/
def Worms : Set (Set ℝ²) :=
    {s | ∃ f : (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 : ℝ)) → ℝ², LipschitzWith 1 f ∧ Set.range f = s}

/--
The set of covers is the set of (measurable) sets
that cover every worm by translation and rotation.
-/
def WormCovers : Set (Set ℝ²) :=
    {X | MeasurableSet X ∧ ∀ w ∈ Worms, ∃ (e : ℝ² ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ²) (v : ℝ²),
      e.toLinearEquiv.det = 1 ∧ w ⊆ (fun x => e x + v) '' X}

/--
A disc of radius 1 / 2 is a worm cover.

This follows by translating the center of the disc to the midpoint of the worm.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 52]
theorem disc_mem_worm_covers : Metric.closedBall 0 0.5 ∈ WormCovers := by
  refine ⟨measurableSet_closedBall, ?_⟩
  rintro w ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨LinearIsometryEquiv.refl ℝ _, f ⟨1/2, by constructor <;> norm_num⟩,
    LinearEquiv.det_refl .., ?_⟩
  rintro _ ⟨t, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨f t - f ⟨1/2, by constructor <;> norm_num⟩, ?_, by simp⟩
  simp only [Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right]
  have h := hf.dist_le_mul t ⟨1/2, by constructor <;> norm_num⟩
  simp only [NNReal.coe_one, one_mul] at h
  rw [dist_eq_norm] at h
  refine h.trans ?_
  obtain ⟨t, ht1, ht2⟩ := t
  simp only [Subtype.dist_eq, Real.dist_eq]
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor <;> linarith

/--
**Moser's Worm Problem**
What is the minimal area (or greatest lower bound on the area)
of a shape that can cover every unit-length curve?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem mosers_worm_problem :
    IsGLB {v | ∃ X ∈ WormCovers, volume X = v} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
There is a set of area 0.260437 that covers all worms.

*Reference:*
Norwood, Rick; Poole, George (2003), "An improved upper bound for Leo Moser's worm problem",
Discrete and Computational Geometry, 29 (3): 409–417, doi:10.1007/s00454-002-0774-3, MR 1961007.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem mosers_worm_problem_upper_bound :
    ∃ X ∈ WormCovers, volume X = 0.260437 := by
  sorry

/--
**Convex Moser's Worm Problem**
What is the minimal area (or greatest lower bound on the area)
of a *convex* shape that can cover every unit-length curve?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem convex_mosers_worm_problem :
    IsGLB {v | ∃ X ∈ WormCovers, Convex ℝ X ∧ volume X = v} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
The minimal area of a convex shape that can cover every unit-length curve is attained.
This follows from the Blaschke selection theorem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem convex_mosers_worm_problem_bound_attained :
    ∃ bound, IsLeast {v | ∃ X ∈ WormCovers, Convex ℝ X ∧ volume X = v} bound := by
  sorry

/--
There is a convex set of area 0.270911861 that covers all worms.

*Reference:*
Wang, Wei (2006), "An improved upper bound for the worm problem",
Acta Mathematica Sinica, 49 (4): 835–846, MR 2264090.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem convex_mosers_worm_problem_upper_bound :
    ∃ X : Set ℝ², MeasurableSet X ∧ Convex ℝ X ∧ volume X = 0.270911861 ∧
      ∀ w ∈ Worms, ∃ (e : ℝ² ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ²) (v : ℝ²), e.toLinearEquiv.det = 1 ∧ w ⊆ (fun x => e x + v) '' X := by
  sorry

/--
0.232239 is a lower bound on the area of a convex set that covers all worms.

*Reference:*
Khandhawit, Tirasan; Pagonakis, Dimitrios; Sriswasdi, Sira (2013),
"Lower Bound for Convex Hull Area and Universal Cover Problems",
International Journal of Computational Geometry & Applications,
23 (3): 197–212, arXiv:1101.5638, doi:10.1142/S0218195913500076, MR 3158583, S2CID 207132316.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem convex_mosers_worm_problem_lower_bound :
    0.232239 ∈ lowerBounds {v | ∃ X ∈ WormCovers, Convex ℝ X ∧ volume X = v} := by
  sorry

end MoserWorm

reformulations.difference: The covering family consists of ranges of 1-Lipschitz maps on [0,1], including curves shorter than one, whereas the sources speak of unit-length rectifiable curves.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A 1-Lipschitz map on [0,1] has length at most one. Conversely, every continuous rectifiable curve of length at most one admits an arclength parametrization, extended constantly to [0,1], with the same range. Every shorter curve can also be extended at an endpoint to a curve of length exactly one. Thus covering all unit-length curves is equivalent to covering every member of Worms. The feasible covers and their areas are unchanged; the argument also applies to the convex variant.

reformulations.difference: Lean requires the worm to lie inside a rotated and translated cover, rather than requiring a rotated and translated worm to lie inside the fixed cover.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The inverse of x ↦ e x + v is y ↦ e.symm y - e.symm v. Its linear part still has determinant one. Applying this inverse converts either containment into the other. The full existential-containment equivalence, and its use in WormCovers, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The numerical upper bound is expressed as existence of a cover of area exactly 0.260437, rather than existence of a cover of area at most that number.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For this finite bound, existence at exactly that area is equivalent to existence at most that area: covering is preserved by taking measurable supersets, and a finite-area measurable set can be enlarged to any prescribed larger finite area by adding a measurable subset of its complement. Norwood–Poole explicitly state in §3, p. 413, that their constructed cover has area less than 0.2604370, so the exact-area existential does not identify its witness with their slightly smaller construction.

reformulations.difference: The convex upper bound is likewise stated using an exact area, 0.270911861.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite-area convex worm cover has positive area: it must contain a congruent copy of a noncollinear bent unit worm and therefore its positive-area triangular convex hull. Given a convex cover of area a ≤ b, dilate about a point of the cover by sqrt(b/a). The factor is at least one, so convexity makes the dilated set contain the original cover; its area is exactly b. The reverse implication to an at-most bound is immediate. Wang's publisher abstract explicitly reports the stated numerical upper bound.

review.notes: Checked both definitions and all seven theorems. The scratch file compiles without errors and verifies empty-set exclusions, constant worms, compactness of worms, finite feasible areas, uniqueness of the GLB, the lower-bound direction, and the attainment statement's quantifiers. It also proves that measurable hulls preserve attainable cover areas, and that taking closures does the same for convex covers, resolving the Borel/Lebesgue measurability distinction. The decimal literals were confirmed to be exact nonnegative-rational casts. Wikipedia still records both optimization problems as open; its stronger 2021 convex upper bound does not invalidate the historical bound or its solved status. Wang's statement was checked against the publisher's bilingual abstracts; the full PDF was unavailable.
